defect.summary: GATE 1's CEILINGS DO NOT SAY THAT A REGION IS A SPELLING, NOT A DIRECTORY. The bridge places a target in a declared region by a byte-for-byte prefix compare, and its canonicaliser does not fold case. On a case-insensitive mount (WSL's /mnt/c, drvfs) one directory has many spellings, so a target spelt in another case than its region's prefix is not placed in that region: it falls to an enclosing region or "/" when one is declared (a coarser category), and is UNDERIVED only when no declared prefix matches it. The loader's duplicate check is byte-exact too, so two spellings of one directory can be declared as two regions with two categories. None of the fourteen ceiling lines says this, so a reader of the envelope takes a region for the directory it names.
defect.ground: The bridge at b12b980 (the line the live bridge runs), read at bytes: mica-bridge/interest-label.ts deriveInterestLabel (prefix p matches target t iff p === "/" or t === p or t starts with p + "/"; longest wins); mica-bridge/target-fingerprint.ts canonicaliseTargetIdentity (NFC, trim, collapse "//", strip one trailing "/"; its header: it "does not case-fold"); mica-bridge/declarations.ts region loader (duplicate prefixes caught by an exact-string set). The pure function was probed at b12b980's bytes (interest-label.ts sha256 6e1a5a079fc7…): same case -> the region; other case, that region alone -> UNDERIVED; other case under a declared enclosing region -> the enclosing region; other case with "/" declared -> "/"'s category; two spellings declared -> each spelling to its own category. T28 condition 9: the ceilings are carried on every surface, and the envelope is bounded by what they say.
